text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Realtime latency regression detected for route `/v1/generate` (prod-us-west-1). p95 crossed 800ms (SLO=600ms), p99=2.30s (SLO=1.5s). Alert ID: ALRT-2003456. Auto-page: @irene oncall.

irene: oncall here, ACKing the page. Pulling dashboards now — jumping to traces and SRE logs. Can others confirm if this is global or region-specific?

sam: seeing pronounced tail spikes on the streaming-serving pool in us-west-1. p99 jump aligns with GPU node set {gpu-5,gpu-7}. Queue depth for streaming connector jumped ~6x. Quick grafana query I ran:```promql
rate(serve_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])
```

anya: also seeing increased prefix-cache miss rate ~+40% in the same window. That increases KV recompute overhead on subsequent tokens. Two suggested immediate mitigations: 1) route a small % to a cheaper per-request model (rw-medium-quant) as a canary, 2) temporarily scale pool by +2 replicas.

incident-bot: Automated mitigation applied: routing policy updated -> route 10% traffic for `/v1/generate` to model `rw-medium-quant` (canary). Monitoring quality guardrails.

miguel: pushed a manual scaling bump to serve-prod-us-west-1: `rctl scale pool/serve-prod-us-west-1 --add 2` (started). Will watch pod boot times.

alex: checking node metrics — gpu-5 shows sustained high GPU memory pressure and KV-cache evictions: log snippet:```text
[17:03:21] kv_cache: evict shard 42 (size 1.2GB)
[17:03:21] recompute: reloading kv shard 42 from disk, 220ms
[17:03:22] request wait: queue_depth=18
```

rui: found a slow trace: trace_id=trace-0x9f1a; timeline: long wait on disk read for KV shard prior to model forward. Looks like increased I/O on the node causing stall before tensor compute. Link to trace: https://internal-grafana/redwood/traces/trace-0x9f1a

irene: customer impact check — CS: how many customers?

customer-success: watching ticket stream — 14 distinct customers reported timeouts over last 15m, 3 enterprise tenants reported degraded availability (Atlas Health, NimbusPayments, BrightEd). Opening support incident notes and sending initial notif.

sam: quick ops question: anyone object to a rolling restart of gpu-5 to clear kernel/GPU cache pressure? Restart should be non-disruptive if traffic routing can be kept away for a minute. :+1: from me if no blockers.

anya: do it. also enable degraded streaming mode (turn off chunked streaming to reduce per-token overhead and queue churn). Command to flip: `rb toggle streaming.degraded_mode --env prod --region us-west-1`.

miguel: initiating restart: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/serve-gpu-5 -n serve-prod` (started at 17:06:10 UTC).

ops-bot: Restart finished for pods in serve-gpu-5 (uptime 1m10s). Health checks passed.

incident-bot: After restart + routing mitigation + scale bump: p95=620ms, p99=1.70s (was p99=2.30s). Continuing to observe.

irene: good improvement. Keep mitigations for 30m and monitor for recurrence. I'll create incident ticket and capture initial timeline. INC-20200345 created.

alex: additional note — audit logs show a config change introduced at 17:02 UTC to `serve-config.kv_cache_size` on pool `serve-prod` which decreased the cache size by ~30%. That would explain the cache miss spike.

sam: can we confirm who deployed that change? run: `rb audit list --resource serve-config --since 17:00 --until 17:10`.

miguel: that was me — I pushed a test config earlier and it accidentally hit the prod namespace during my test window. Sorry all, reverting now.

ops-bot: Config revert completed: `serve-config.kv_cache_size` restored to previous value.

incident-bot: Metrics 10m after revert: p95=590ms, p99=1.20s. Immediate mitigation closed.

rui: starting an automatic eval comparing `rw-medium-quant` output vs primary to ensure no hidden quality regression from the canary routing. Will pause routing if eval drift > 3%.

irene: excellent. Action items from this thread: 1) Postmortem owner: miguel (to document accidental config push). 2) Add a gate to prevent kv-cache config drift into prod (owner: infra). 3) Add automated detection for rapid drops in kv_cache_size tied to latency alarms (owner: SRE). 4) Adjust realtime-alerting to raise earlier on kv-cache-config diffs. I'll schedule a 30m follow-up huddle.

customer-success: notified impacted customers with ETA for full postmortem. Will update once PMs post the timeline.

impressions: :thumbsup: from team. Closing on-call handoff in 35m unless recurrence.

-- end of thread --
